channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: A reality check hits Africa’s richest country as it begins the year on a cautious note
item.description: Notwithstanding a year of unprecedented economic performance in South Africa, underscored by a five-year peak in job creation and an estimated Gross Domestic Product of $410 billion, the nation has commenced the current year with a dampened economic sentiment.

item.title: Moroccan billionaire Anas Sefrioui commits $300m to luxury Abidjan development
item.description: Moroccan property billionaire, Anas Sefrioui is committing more than MAD 3 billion (about $300 million) to a major mixed-use development in Abidjan, marking one of his most significant investments yet in Côte d’Ivoire’s commercial capital.

item.title: Ghana pays $910m in debt exchange interest as market opens for US, EU, and other investors
item.description: Ghana has paid 10 billion cedis, equivalent to about $910 million, in interest under its Domestic Debt Exchange Programme, marking the sixth coupon settlement since the country began restructuring its obligations during its worst economic crisis in a generation.

item.title: IFC launches $10 million deal to unlock $20 million in SME lending in Ethiopia
item.description: IFC has announced a new $10 million partnership with Dashen Bank S.C. to boost lending for small and medium-sized businesses in Ethiopia. The move is designed to unlock up to $20 million in new credit for entrepreneurs, especially those working in agribusiness and those running women-owned or women-led companies.

item.title: 10 African countries with the weakest naval fleets in 2026
item.description: One of Africa's most expensive blind spots is its inadequate naval capability.

item.title: Growing black prosperity alters South Africa’s wealth demographics more than 30 years after apartheid
item.description: Rising earnings among Black South Africans have significantly changed the racial makeup of the country’s middle- and top-income households over the three decades since the end of apartheid.

item.title: US tariffs make South African wine costlier in the world’s biggest wine market
item.description: Tariffs on South African agricultural products imposed by the United States are driving up the cost of South African wine in the world’s largest market.

item.title: U.S. gains access to world’s richest tantalum deposit in DR Congo as mineral deal reshapes war, global tech supply chains
item.description: The United States is positioning itself at the center of one of the world’s most strategic mineral regions after securing access to the Democratic Republic of Congo’s vast tantalum reserves, part of a broader push to stabilize the conflict-hit country while strengthening Western control over critical mineral supply chains.

item.title: Niger secures $91 million IMF boost as AES states regain global financial recognition
item.description: Niger’s military-led government has secured fresh external financing in a move that highlights the country’s continued access to global financial support despite its political realignment and growing role in the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

item.title: UAE targets deeper Zambia trade as bilateral trade hits $3.4 billion
item.description: Trade and investment ties between the United Arab Emirates and Zambia are poised to expand following high-level talks in Lusaka between senior officials from both countries.
